You'll lose sight of it and instead find some creepy effigy thing standing beside a tree. Check it out, get stink-apacitated, and get your not so informative close-up sighting of bigfoot's big feet.

After your sighting, keep your eyes peeled for flyers about the skunk ape posted on storefronts and telephone poles around Leonida. They'll lead you to a mission where you can learn more about the mysterious beast.

#3719. Infinity Nikki Players Are Planning To ‘Girl-cott’ The Game Over Maye Musk Ad

Infold Games, developers of Love and Deepspace and Infinity Nikki, are 0 for 2 in pissing off their international fanbase for both games. Earlier this year, the studio announced, then cancelled, Love and Deepspace‘s sixth love interest, the werewolf Valko, inspiring some players to go on a sustained boycott that seems to have had a noticeable impact on the gacha game’s revenue in the months since. Now some Infinity Nikki players are hoping to achieve a similar effect, planning a “girl-cott” after Chinese ads for the dress-up gacha game featured Maye Musk, mom of noted racist and transphobe Elon Musk.

Beyond the practical discussions of how exactly to inform Infold Games of player dissatisfaction, girl-cott conversations on the Infinity Nikki subreddit have devolved into thorny back-and-forths on where to draw the line about the thing you enjoy. Some players can’t play the game in good conscience, knowing that Infold Games would choose to partner with the mother of guy who said he fed the USAID organization, responsible for providing food and medical assistance to countries in need, “into the woodchipper,” an act projected to result in widespread death, infection, and suffering for millions, including children. Others don’t see the issue because Maye Musk is not her son, however odious he may be, and the antipathy for him seems to be a uniquely American sentiment with little bearing in the wider, international (and Chinese) Infinity Nikki community.

As a player of both Infinity Nikki and Love and Deepspace, it’s interesting to see both communities arrive at the same fracture point in their relationships with their respective games over two very different events. It’s too early to tell how much of an impact the girl-cott will have, but its timing will no doubt hamper the momentum of the game’s upcoming 3.0 release later this month. If this girl-cott is anything like what happened with Love and Deepspace, Infold Games is once again looking at potential losses in the millions.

#3718. GTA 6 won't let you use cheats until you complete the main story, and locks progression when you do

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

The way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

2026 has been pretty weird, but I wasn't expecting a dino sighting.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I thought we'd already gotten our fill of prehistoric creatures on the 2026 movie schedule, thanks to The End of Oak Street. The film sees Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor spending a summer trying to survive a neighborhood full of creatures that should have been extinct for millions of years. Then, as soon as the movie hit streaming, the internet started arguing over footage supposedly showing a pterodactyl flying over Mexico. The timing feels a little too perfect.

The latest monster-of-the-week discussion took off on November 13, when someone posted images to Reddit's r/Cryptozoology forum. The poster claimed the winged creature had been caught on airport security footage in Ciudad Juárez and that additional witnesses had photographs. None of that was verified, but you can probably guess how the comments went.

I'll give the image this much: It's pretty cool. The creature has an enormous wingspan, a long, pointed head, and a silhouette you'd expect to see flying over the Platt family's house in The End of Oak Street. Of course, it also looks suspiciously like something you'd find in Jurassic Park. Several Reddit users noticed that resemblance, too, and weren't particularly convinced.

There's apparently more to the sighting. According to Mexican outlet El Financier, an earlier video, reportedly recorded October 29 in the Anapra area of Ciudad Juárez, shows a mysterious winged figure flying across the night sky. Jaime Maussan, a Mexican broadcaster known for his interest in UFOs and other unexplained phenomena, picked up the footage and helped spread the story. Before long, additional alleged sightings circulated online, and naturally, the internet had a field day.

No cryptic sighting is worth its weight in dino dung unless the internet loses its collective mind, and the comments weren't disappointing. One commenter with the username r/alfred0t0rnad0 pretty much summed up my feelings:

Somebody else was considerably more enthusiastic about the possibility of prehistoric creatures making a comeback. R/AsadAliShadowhunter wrote:

At this point, I hope the Dinos are back.

Look, I'm not opposed to a little prehistoric excitement. I'd just prefer anything with a 20-foot wingspan to stay away from my backyard.

Those two comments barely scratch the surface, though. Some users had legitimate questions about the footage, while others were just enjoying the absurdity. Here are a few of my favorites:

Personally, I'm partial to the idea of a prehistoric creature emerging from the hollow Earth for tacos. But the commenters questioning how an entire population of giant flying reptiles could have gone unnoticed for millions of years have a pretty good point.

The End Of Oak Street Ending: Yes, They Had Conversations About The Dog Dying

There's also the small matter of what local authorities have said about the footage. EFE's fact-checking team reported Wednesday that Ciudad Juárez's civil protection director, Sergio Rodríguez, dismissed the recordings as digital entertainment content. One widely shared version also appears to show signs of AI manipulation, although the origins of the various clips haven't all been established.

Unfortunately for those of us hoping The End of Oak Street had somehow become a documentary, there's no credible evidence that a pterodactyl is flying around Mexico. Still, I have to admit I've enjoyed watching the internet speculate over the possibility.

The End of Oak Street is now streaming with an HBO Max subscription, which makes it an excellent choice if this whole thing has you craving some cinematic dinosaurs.

The game "outperformed expectations in its launch quarter"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ubisoft just laid off another 166 developers, the latest wave in a months-long tsunami of job cuts that also includes some of the devs behind Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced. Yet the company's latest financial report brags of impressive financial success, driven by the popularity of the remake.

"Net bookings stood at €389m this quarter, above guidance of around €370m," the company says in its new earnings release, which marks a "50% year-on-year" increase. "The outperformance was mainly driven by Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced," Ubisoft says, also acknowledging "strong performances" from catalog sales of Assassin's Creed and Ghost Recon games, as well as its Invincible mobile game.

Ubisoft's superlatives don't stop there, either. "Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced outperformed expectations in its launch quarter," the release continues, "supported by solid in-game spending and a higher-than-expected share of premium editions. The game’s performance also benefited from a more targeted marketing approach."

Black Flag Resynced was one of the first games to be launched after the Ubisoft's "major reset," which saw the company cancel and delay a multitude of games as it restructured its studios under five "creative houses."

Ubisoft says, "Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced illustrates its ability to deliver games that players love and that also perform financially. The newly formed Assassin’s Creed leadership made clear, decisive choices in the final stretch of development. This enabled the game to achieve an elevated level of quality and a commercial performance that positions Black Flag Resynced among the industry’s most successful Action-Adventure remakes."

The company doesn't specify which action-adventure remakes it's comparing against here, but nowadays the statement certainly invites a thought toward Nintendo's wildly successful remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Black Flag Resynced's 3.5 million sales in two weeks is no match for Zelda's 5.2 million sales in four days, but who knows how the post-launch sales measure against each other.

Still, all that financial success isn't enough to slow down Ubisoft's "rightsizing" operation, which has seen another 1,100 jobs disappear from the company in the past six months alone. Ubisoft has been warning shareholders that losing "key talents and skills" is a big danger for the company, but that hasn't stopped it from cutting many of the developers responsible for its most successful games.

#3714. Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

Sandy Petersen is wishing someone else well for a change.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As reported by GamesRadar, former id Software developer Sandy Petersen recently took to Twitter to make an impassioned defense of Valve founder Gabe Newell. Petersen was responding to discussion of how Newell's apparent good treatment of his crew is a rarity among superyacht enthusiasts. Here's Petersen's full statement:

"I know Gabe Newell. We have chatted at some length. I know numerous men who worked for him as well. I am sure that there must be some disgruntled ex-employees out there but everyone I know who has dealt with him respects and admires him.

"And with Steam he is literally guarding the gates of Hell⁠—preserving all gamers from the horrors of what would happen if parasites like Disney, EA, or Microsoft became the providers.

I don't think I disagree with anything Petersen said here: I certainly have criticisms of Valve, but it has been a uniquely positive force in games. I don't think PC gaming would be what it is today if a company like EA or Microsoft had beat Valve to the punch on digital distribution in the late 2000s.

There's always room for improvement, but I tend to prioritize Valve's management of Steam over concerns about its internal game development culture. If I could change one thing about the company, it would be lowering the 30% cut it takes from every game sold on Steam.

Valve punches well above its approximate 340-person headcount (336 at last call, but that was five years ago and before it absorbed Risk of Rain dev Hopoo Games). It is, pound for pound, possibly one of the most profitable companies to ever exist⁠—compare its outsized role in the industry, outperforming massive companies like EA and Ubisoft, to its relatively small size. Valve employees, by all accounts, are well-renumerated for their labor.

But I always find it uncomfortable to consider Valve's historic megaprofits and Newell's personal fortune while so many studios are struggling to remain solvent. The company would likely retain its world-historic profitability with a smaller or more graduated cut of each game sale, something the Epic Store implemented long ago, and which remains a strong talking point for Tim Sweeney's Steam competitor.

This isn't just a question of pure altruism: Steam requires a healthy development ecosystem to thrive as it does. Each studio that stays open instead of closing, each bedroom programmer who can quit their day job for indie development full time, is a future moneymaker for Valve. You get leaner, but more sustainable profit.

At the same time, even Valve's relatively high cut of sales was a massive improvement from the world of physical, retail games. And whatever gripes developers have about Steam, it is the fan-favorite PC platform for a reason: It is the only online or social media platform of comparable reach and vintage that has not been thoroughly enshittified⁠—had its usability compromised in the name of short-term profits.

Even with increasing amounts of AI shovelware on the platform and frustrating, inconsistent content moderation, it always feels like Valve is operating in good faith as a steward of the hobby, and I find that extremely precious and worth celebrating on the internet of 2026.

Completely changing the subject, I would be remiss if I failed to mention the thing that Petersen is most famous for after his work on Doom and Quake: John Romero wishing him well. Former PCG editor Wes Fenlon compiled a short history of Petersen making social media statements about the history of id Software, only to have company co-founder John Romero politely correct him.

#3712. GTA 6's Japanese version only partially obscures male nudity by putting Jason in a thong, seemingly due to regional censorship

GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and New Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ

Another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. Among the book-to-screen adaptations I'm most excited for in 2027 is The Nightingale. Based on Kristin Hannah's brilliant novel, the story follows two sisters in France whose lives go in different directions during World War II, and the choices they have to make along the way.

Directed by Michael Morris and starring real-life sisters Dakota and Elle Fanning, The Nightingale follows their characters' stories as they find themselves getting more involved in what's going around them as the Nazis invade France. While Hannah's novel is historical fiction, the book is inspired by true accounts of the war.

The more I've learned about World War II, particularly in looking at the impact it had on different regions of the world, the more interested I've become in hearing stories about the involvement of women in the war. Naturally, I was drawn to Hannah's novel. (She also wrote an amazing historical fiction novel called The Women, which is set during the Vietnam War that I highly recommend.) Exciting, emotional and powerful, The Nightingale absolutely lived up to the hype (4.6+ out of 5 on Goodreads with over 2 million ratings?!), and I can't wait to see the movie.

In The Nightingale, Vianne (Dakota Fanning) is trying to keep her daughter safe as the Nazis begin to occupy France. Meanwhile, her younger sister, Isabelle (Elle Fanning), wants to take a more active role in what's going on, and finds herself joining the resistance. While both sisters take a very different approach to survival during this turbulent and dangerous time, the story really shows the way courage can emerge in different ways.

With just a minute's worth of footage, this new teaser gives us a good look at what these two sisters face as their entire world is upended by this war. Vianne is determined to keep her family safe, while Isabelle -- despite her very young age -- can't stand by and not try to help make a difference. In the end, both women end up finding themselves faced with dangerous situations and impossible choices that require quick thinking and more courage than most could muster when push comes to shove. Whether they're protecting children and innocents or going undercover to help with the resistance, the story of these sisters shows the impact one woman can make amidst the chaos of war.

Of course, the teaser leaves off with "She'll need a codename," which points directly to the title of the movie.

I'm excited about everything to do with this adaptation, from the source material, to the stars, to what we're seeing here. While many World War II movies emphasize the invasions and battles, stories like The Nightingale -- whether fiction, non-fiction, or inspired by true events -- remind us of the impact of war on the spaces in between the battles, and the civilians who find (sometimes crucial) ways to help.

The Nightingale is set to hit theaters on the 2027 movie schedule on March 19, 2027.

The 2TB model will be "especially constrained": Valve has closed the waitlist and says it doesn't know how many it will be able to make, or at what price they'll be sold.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them.

Valve has good news and bad news for anyone interested in buying a Steam Machine. All current reservations for the 512GB model have been fulfilled and there's stock remaining, so if you want one you can just head over to the purchase page and buy it—but the 2TB model is in shorter supply so signups for the waitlist are no longer being taken.

And, sorry to say, there's also worse news: Valve says it won't be able to produce them in the quantities it had planned, and the price could increase.

Despite their high prices, demand for Steam Machines was high enough that Valve implemented a randomized lottery system to buy one: Prospective purchasers signed up for a shot, a randomized selection were put in a reservation queue with a Steam Machine reserved in their name, and everyone else went to the waiting list to be notified when more reservation spots came open.

Valve said in July that it expected to have the reservation queue caught up by the end of 2026, and that's now the case with the 512GB model: They're in an "an add-to-cart status," meaning that while supplies last, you can purchase one and it will be shipped straight away.

The situation is less happy for people waiting for the 2TB model, though. In an update posted today, Valve said all reservation holders have been sent their invitations to purchase but there are still people on the waiting list; those people won't lose their positions, but no one else will be allowed to join.

It sounds like that situation is likely to hold for at least a few months, as Valve said it expects to have more information on additional supply of the 2TB units to share in January. It also invited people on the waitlist to purchase a 512GB model instead, but warned that they'll lose their spot on the 2TB waitlist if they do.

Nobody likes to downgrade, and 512GB isn't as spacious as it used to be: Phantom Blade Zero requires an astronomical 300GB of free space for its pre-install process. While that's a bit of an outlier, games eating up more than 100GB of storage are very common these days. But Steam Machines are being hammered as much as anyone by the RAMpocalypse, and Valve said that's not changing anytime soon.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

"We are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts," Valve wrote in today's update. "For Steam Machine, that is especially impacting the 2TB model, where the number of customers on the waitlist exceeds our current production; even when we are able to build more it will be at smaller quantities than we planned."

It repeated that message in its conclusion: "We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained."

Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is headed back to theaters

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Christopher Nolan says there are plenty of deleted scenes from The Odyssey, but that we won't be seeing them anytime soon.

"There’s a lot of deleted scenes scrumpled up in the wastebasket that no one will ever see," Nolan told The Independent. "I don’t really believe in director’s cuts. I want to stand by the film that goes out. As a writer-director, I try to do a lot of that weeding out. There aren’t many scenes that were shot."

Continued Nolan: "On a film like this, to spend a day shooting something on top of a mountain or in the rain or on a boat or whatever that isn’t gonna be in the film, I would really rather not do that. And so I wanna stand behind the cuts of the films that are put out there.”

The film hit theaters on July 17, stayed on premium large format screens until September 30, got another release in October, and will have one last IMAX 70mm release in December. It earned over $1.8 billion at the global box office, which officially makes it the highest-grossing R-rated movie of all time.

The nearly three-hour-long movie was finally released on premium VOD, 4K, and DVD this week... and we're sad that there are no special deleted scenes included in the release. We can only imagine that a Nolan-style director's cut would put the film up to four, or even four-and-a-half hours, and yet I'd probably still go out to see that in 4DX.

#3706. It really seems like Xbox isn't allowed to say GTA 6 at all

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the big release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

"Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is important. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either."

One day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe."

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

So what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

This is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

For all intents and purposes, Taylor Swift’s performance during the CMA Awards telecast on the 2026 TV schedule honored her song in Toy Story 5. Seemingly, another great step in her Oscar campaign, the actress sang “I Knew It, I Knew You” and mashed it up with “Our Song.” That mashup made me think for a bit that an announcement for Taylor Swift (Taylor’s Version) might happen as well…but it didn’t. However, just because an announcement wasn’t made doesn’t mean Swifties weren’t spiraling over this performance, especially after clocking a vital detail.

As per usual, Taylor Swift’s performance was very meaningful and packed with surprises. From Jessie’s tree in Toy Story 5 being the background of her stage to the ensemble of A-list country superstars she assembled for the backstage portion, there was a lot to take in. However, I want to focus on the first thing we saw during the number, when the pop star was standing in her dressing room. Take a look:

In the image above, you can see a rack of dresses behind Taylor Swift on her left; there’s a Jessie doll on her couch, and then there are a few gowns to her right. The dress at the front of the rack is the one the singer wore to the Academy of Country Music Awards in 2006. Meanwhile, the yellow gown on the couch seems to be the dress she wore to the 41st CMA Awards in 2007, and the green one next to it appears to be what she rocked at the CMT Music Awards the same year. Then, there’s the blue dress falling off the couch, which I’d guess is her gown from the “Our Song” music video.

Alright, folks, that’s a whole lot of Debut Easter eggs in one frame, and it pairs suspiciously well with the fact that Swift did mash up “I Knew It, I Knew You” with “Our Song.”

Of course, Taylor Swift is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year, so this could all be an homage to that. However, Swifties, obviously, are freaking out and think there might be more to it, as they were reacting with comments like:

Yeah, it’s really hard not to read into all those dresses, and of course, that’s what fans are doing. Between Swift’s reputation for Easter eggs that allude to what’s next and her tendency to surprise fans with announcements, this certainly feels like it's leading up to something.

Obviously, it could just be part of her Oscar campaign for her Toy Story 5 song and an innocent homage to her first album, which turned 20 this year. Plus, we’ve clowned many times before about Taylor Swift (Taylor’s Version) and been wrong. However, I’m familiar with this Mastermind’s games, and these dresses really make me (and the Swifties) think she’s up to something.

Here's what's true and what isn't true about these misleading Grand Theft Auto 6 claims.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As players explore Leonida for the first time, misleading claims about Grand Theft Auto 6 have begun circulating on social media as evidence that Rockstar has toned down the series' violence. The two claims I've seen most often are along the lines of:

Both of these claims are misleading half-truths.

⛔ No, because there is no gay or LGBTQ nightclub in GTA 6.

It is true that you cannot use firearms inside of GTA 6 clubs, such as Nine1nine and The Vault. Grand Theft Auto 5 had the same restriction. But none of the clubs in GTA 6 are specifically presented as gay or LGBTQ clubs.

It is reasonable to speculate that Rockstar would want to avoid in-game scenarios that closely resemble the 2016 Pulse nightclub shooting in Florida—the state Leonida parodies—but the studio has not stated as much.

⛔ No, unless you've turned on a setting which reduces vehicle damage.

Clips of Grand Theft Auto 6 airplanes smacking into tall buildings without taking any apparent damage have been used on social media to claim that Rockstar is intentionally preventing players from replicating 9/11-like crashes, or that the vehicle physics are shoddy.

The clips of ultra-strong planes aren't fake, but are achieved by turning on "Reduced Vehicle Damage" in the gameplay settings.

In the menu, Rockstar warns players that turning the setting on will "significantly change the balance and experience of gameplay."

If you fly into a building without reduced vehicle damage, your plane will explode. It doesn't damage the building, but there's nothing to indicate that Rockstar has manipulated vehicle physics to avoid recalling terrorism.

"Its current focus is on new player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While the industry debates the value of using generative AI as a behind-the-scenes development tool, Ubisoft is leaping over that fence. The company has tripled down on its intention to put player-facing generative AI in its games, announcing the establishment of a new subsidiary called Motherbrain, which is "focused on AI for gameplay innovation."

Motherbrain "has been established as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technology for new forms of gameplay. Its current focus is on new player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds," Ubisoft says in its latest financial report. "It aims to serve creators globally, both within Ubisoft’s Creative House ecosystem and beyond, and form partnerships with selected technology actors."

Ubisoft has been talking up the idea of NPCs powered by generative AI for years, going back to an effort called Project NEO NPC, which built characters that could respond to players like an LLM-powered chatbot with its own backstory. By 2025, that effort had evolved into Teammates, a prototype shooter built around a squad of companions that respond to "real-time voice commands" and "adapt their behavior to each situation, revealing distinct personalities along the way."

Now, the Teammates devs are now heading Motherbrain. Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot hopes that Motherbrain's work will "open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences."

All this comes amid mass layoffs at Ubisoft. The company says its headcount was down to 15,500 as of September 2026. That's an eye-watering number in itself, but it's a massive reduction in people from 20,700 in September 2022. Ubisoft says it's cut 1,100 jobs in the past six months alone.

The extent to which AAA developers are already using generative AI to create games is not fully clear to us on the outside, though certainly there are people, like Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who are keen to suggest it's already nigh-ubiquitous. But AI generating in-game content live for players is much rarer, outside of Epic's own AI Darth Vader, which instantly started spouting slurs.

Back in 2025, Guillemot presented his own vision for games with built-in AI content generation. "For players, the world will react to their behavior instead of pre-scripted things," he said. "We have been creating open worlds in the past, giving more choices to payers, and now we will go another step further, which is, OK, [to] make sure that you have an impact on the world, and the world will react to you. So it will be your world."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Some players will look at the possibility of a game world with infinite, responsive content as something magical. Personally? I've played several of Ubisoft's 100-hour open-world epics to completion, and I know even human developers can struggle to populate these worlds with engaging stories and things to do. It's tough to imagine a chatbot version of Socrates offering an experience worth remembering.

#3700. GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

Uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are currently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more."

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

As popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the company has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

#3699. The hunt for World of Warcraft: Forever secrets continue with the discovery of an elusive pet

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a new breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this new pet.

The way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

So what's the big deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

This is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Frankie wants to know if you can dance, yes or no. What should you say?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

You'll face a choice in Chapter 2 of GTA 6, when you're ready to help Vicky rob her boss, Frankie, at the Delights strip club in Port Gellhorn. Frankie asks you an important question and you've only got a couple seconds to respond:

"Can you dance? Yes or no, dude?" Frankie has caught you (as Jason) coming in the back door of the club as you and Lucia prepare to rob it. It's ladies night and one of the male strippers is out of commission, but Mario, the lead stripper, gets an idea when he meets Jason. Frankie has the same idea, and asks if Jason knows how to dance.

Yes, they are asking Jason if he can fill in as a male stripper for the show.

Personally, both versions are worth seeing, but Jason playing a stripper, and Lucia's utter delight at seeing him play a stripper, is way more fun.

Let's talk about why the coin flip doesn't work.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There’s a really obvious problem with Survivor’s Coin Flip. The new game mechanic that was introduced last season gives one player a chance to double the prize pot and earn themselves an idol if they call a coin flip correctly or sends them home immediately if they don't. In theory, it's a high stakes game of chance that should make for exciting television, but there's an inherent structural issue that doesn't play well with network television.

The episode runtime spoiled the result of last night’s coin flip, just as it spoiled the result of Rick Devens’ coin flip on 50, just as it will likely spoil the results of any coin flip the show does in the future. Every episode ends with someone going home; so, if there’s a few minutes left when the person flips the coin, it’s bad news for them. If there’s enough time to do an entire vote after they flip the coin, it’s good news for them.

It’s an obvious problem and one that’s very valid for fans to complain about, but it’s actually not my biggest problem with the coin flip twist. I want it gone because it creates the potential to send someone home without being voted out.

Yes, sometimes people go home because they quit or get medically evacuated (get better soon, New England Rob), but that’s a natural byproduct of trying to survive in harsh conditions, not a production decision to try and generate drama. Yes, when there are four players left, we get a fire-making competition instead of a traditional vote, but that at least feels on brand to the show and also, is the subject of fan protests every single season. This coin flip thing, however, feels entirely different. It feels like a wacky gameshow element producers inserted because wouldn’t that make for fun television?

As a Survivor fan, however, I don’t think it makes for fun television. I am watching the show because I want to see the castaways actually play the social strategic game they signed up for. I want to see them try to navigate the island and their competitors and figure out how to survive each tribal council using the tools at their disposal. I don’t want to see one of them do an entirely luck-based challenge to decide their fate. That’s not the point of the game.

To be clear, luck does play a huge role on Survivor. Castaways go home all the time because they’re swapped onto the wrong tribe or their team loses an immunity challenge because other people blow a huge lead on a puzzle or whatever. The game is rarely fair, but in theory, even when it’s unfair, the player still has a chance to wiggle out of whatever danger they’re in. Get swapped onto a tribe against four members of an alliance? Try to find a crack and pit them against each other. Figure out that you’re on the wrong side of the numbers a few hours before tribal council? Go hunt for idols or make a fake idol or do something reckless to try and blow up someone else’s spot.

Those desperate shenanigans usually don’t work, but it still feels like the losing player’s fate was in their own hands. Maybe if they had found the right combination of words. Maybe if they had hunted in a different location. Maybe if they had built better relationships with the other side earlier in the game. Maybe if they had done something else, things would have been different.

You could look at the coin flip and say that’s an example of Survivor giving a player on the bottom a mechanism to change their fate, but to me, flipping a coin just feels so luck-based. It’s like a more obnoxious version of the Shot In The Dark, but at least with the Shot In The Dark, every player is given the same token and can use it in creative ways to build trust, try to avoid using an idol, etc. With the coin flip, it feels like a once a season game of chance for one player to do as part of a special event episode.

I didn’t like the coin flip when Rick Devens did it during 50. I didn’t like it last night when Lewis Kelly did it during 51, and I’m not going to like it next season when some unknown person flips it during 52. Yes, the runtime is an issue, but the bigger problem is it doesn’t feel authentic to the spirit of Survivor and the game they’re playing.

This season has been so good thus far. The characters are fantastic. The gameplay is chaotic. It's a great time, which is why I just want to see everyone play the actual show I signed up to watch.

#3694. GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release

"The decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers."

Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop."

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their plans. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition."

Though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony plans to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

Disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Deciding whether to give the statue to Benedict Halifax is a decision you'll need to make during the fourth story mission of Chapter 3 in GTA 6, called Dubious Provenance. This mission will kick off after Cal visits the Bayside apartment you're borrowing from Boobie to inspect the hard drive.

GTA 6 just might cure the male loneliness epidemic. Wait, why are you laughing? I’m being dead serious. There are moments early in the game where the player, as Jason, is prompted to do something nice for Lucia like buying her flowers or a piece of jewelry. These are optional quests designed for little more than reinforcing the relationship the two have. It’s this element, the game’s continued emphasis on the building and maintenance of the relationship between Jason and Lucia and how it’s a core part of the game, that has the potential to change hearts and minds.

It's been a thrilling week in movie news, largely thanks to confirmation that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's developing blockbuster. Fans have been reacting to this news, but there's also been plenty of discourse about who might be joining the Twilight alum as the villain and/or the next Bond Girl. There are a number of fan choices swirling around online for the latter, and I'm glad folks are already asking these actresses if they'd be down to join the blockbuster.

The James Bond movies (which are streaming with an Amazon Prime subscription) have always had Bond girls. As such, we should expect some femme fatales to join Robert Pattinson in Villeneuve's developing movie. In a recent interview with Variety, actress Gemma Chan was asked about fans who want to see her in this role, responding with:

I’m flattered, and absolutely I would. It’s an iconic franchise, and I’m very excited that things are moving forward with it now.

We love to see it. Chan seems like a great choice to play a Bond girl, not only because she's a prominent British actress. She's also got plenty of action experience, thanks to her roles in both Eternals and Captain Marvel, as well as Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit. The latter doesn't feel far off from a 007 project, and the fact that she'd be down to join the 26th movie in the franchise is thrilling news.

Of course, there's no guarantee that the Five Star Weekend actress is actually being considered. What's more, there are plenty of other names that fans have been tossing around to play the next Bond girl.

Another popular choice from the fan casting perspective has been Sydney Sweeney, whose starpower has been growing for years. She's also trained in karate, kickboxing, and MMA, which could help her in any potential action sequences. Back in October of 2025, Variety asked the Euphoria actress if she'd be down to play a Bond Girl, and she responded with:

Depends on the script. I think I’d have more fun as James Bond.

This wasn't a yes, but it also wasn't a no. I have to wonder if her tune might have changed a year later, especially with Robert Pattinson now officially playing the martini-sipping MI6 agent. Either way, I have to assume that Denis Villeneuve has a number of actresses in mind to play a supporting presence in the 26th Bond movie. Hopefully we get more casting news sooner rather than later.

It's unclear when Bond 26 will hit theaters, but folks are assuming it'll be sometime in 2028. For now, fans can see Denis Villeneuve and Robert Pattinson's collaboration when Dune: Part Three hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list.

#3690. GTA 6 has replaced websites with social media and phone apps because "it didn't feel necessary"

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

The web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

"It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps."

Though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson said the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson said, adding that websites may return in the future.

"I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

"We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," said Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a big shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world."

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore new possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its big heart.

#3688. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was October's biggest game in the US, but it wasn't enough to crack 2026's best-selling top 10

Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other big-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. #3685. As Rockstar's alleged "union busting" tribunal hearing comes to a close amid GTA 6 launch, judge pledges to deliver verdict "as quickly as I possibly can"

Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's currently no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

The case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

People Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can."

However, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog."

One fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they said. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the new depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it."

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

Additionally, Rockstar employees are currently voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week. The next best thing on PC is GTA 5, and its recent Steam concurrents suggest people are trying their best to fight the FOMO until Rockstar decides to bring the new one over.

You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month. SteamDB shows a peak of around 87,000 concurrent players in the last day, an almost 10% increase from October. There's been a bit of a dip today—which could partially be attributed to GTA 6 finally becoming available in every region—but it's not as sharp of a drop as you'd think it'd be for a 13-year-old game.

In fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount. It usually hovers around 40,000 to 50,000 average concurrent players, and GTA 6's release hasn't broken the pattern. That's the beauty of PC gaming for you: Steam sales and mods keep games like this chugging along years after they'd be considered cutting edge.

GTA 5 holdouts might have a long road ahead of them though. GamesBeat reported last month that "four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans" said GTA 6 will make its way to PC in the first three months of 2027. In the past, Rockstar held PC releases back for at least seven months (GTA 5 PC took a year and six months), so an early 2027 release would be unorthodox if the report is true.

GTA Online, or some kind of multiplayer mode, will hopefully come at some point and it would make some sense to drop it at the same time as a PC release, or at least that's what I tell myself at night. I've only played a few hours of the game and I'm already imagining the kinds of mods that will inevitably show up in the first week. Someone is going to make it so Jason can instantly gulp down his coffee for the stamina buff, I know it.

For now, PC players will just have to continue biding their time in GTA 5 and pray that Rockstar at the very least announces a GTA 6 PC release date sooner rather than later.

#3681. Warren Spector lambasts GTA 6's "billion dollar" development - 'I just hope it's is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer'

"A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries."

As GTA 6 finally arrives, increasingly outspoken games industry legend Warren Spector - known for seminal immersive sims including Deus Ex - has offered both praise for the game's achievements and lambasted its "billion dollar" development model, writing, "I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it’s the best we have to offer".

Spector announced his retirement from games development in August following struggles at his OtherSide Entertainment studio, and has been vocal about the state of the games industry in the months since, notably saying anyone at EA responsible for the "travesty" of BioWare's closure should be "ashamed". And now Spector has taken on GTA 6.

"First, congratulations to everyone who worked on GTA 6. It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "However… its billion dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate.

"That's especially true," Spector continued, "when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries. Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is."

The "sure success" of GTA 6 proves a point he's made "for years", he said: "That no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget". Highlighting GTA 6's year-long delay and reported billion dollar budget, Spector suggested, "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready [is] guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has.

"So, again, congratulations," Spector concluded. "Ambition and innovation are necessary for the medium to reach its potential. I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer."

Despite Spector's concerns, GTA 6's arrival is, as expected, already causing shockwaves across the industry. It has broken pre-order records for Xbox and PlayStation stores, smashed the all-time livestream viewer record, and apparently briefly broke Reddit too. And is its success deserved? Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell thinks so, saying it "pushes back the horizon of video games once again" in his five star GTA 6 review.

The changes "range from subtle to more significant"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Lucia and Jason's dynamic relationship is very much the heart and soul of GTA 6's story, offering a nuanced look at a complicated romance that changes based on your decisions in the game. Neglect your relationship and the lovers will drift apart, but nurture it and you'll see it blossom. It's no secret that GTA 6's take on Bonnie and Clyde can separate romantically based on player choice, and that they'll remain partners in crime no matter what, but it turns out pivotal story moments can change significantly based on your relationship status.

Talking to Game Informer, senior design director Luke Howard emphasizes the importance of Lucia and Jason having some sort of relationship with one another even if the romantic spark fizzles out. "This gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist.

"In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile."

Howard uses an example of Lucia pulling off an intense armored truck robbery and Jason pulling her aside to check on her, which is a scene with "several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them.

"The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia," says Howard.

I've only played a few hours of GTA 6 at this point and haven't had the chance to really change the course of Lucia and Jason's relationship, but I can already tell I'm going to become deeply invested in this part of the game thanks to strong writing and performances all around. Am I going to cry playing a GTA game? It sure seems so.

#3679. Does GTA 6 have an 'easy mode'? Not officially, but there are two very important settings you can change to make the game less difficult

By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

Toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

"We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all."

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Queen's Domain has, by my count, four categories of collectible you have to hoover up if you want to see its more hidden endings, and some of them are real bastards to find⁠—I'd resigned myself to queueing up guides on YouTube to get it all done.

Guides are great, you might still need them for some of the collectibles, and if there's one game that feels like it was designed with Google/Reddit/forum help in mind, it's Queen's Domain. But I was thrilled to discover that, very late in the game, Queen's Domain provides a waypoint tool to guide you to its hidden collectibles. It turned what I worried would be a tedious process into yet another example of this game's boundless capacity for surprise and discovery.

I know I would have appreciated the heads-up, the permission to not worry about finding them all earlier in my playtime. If that's how you felt, and you aren't looking for spoilers, great: You can stop reading here. Granted, the spoilers in Queen's Domain are so absurd and out there as to be incomprehensible to someone early on in a playthrough.

There are two requirements to get homing compass guidance in Queen's Domain: You need a fully kitted-out Mask of Second Sight, and to discover the hidden Petrified Garden zone. You can technically reach the latter from very early in the game, but you won't be able to open the necessary path until you acquire all of the lenses for the mask. Here's a quick checklist:

That's basically, like, the entire third act of the game and encompasses most of the requirements for Queen's Domain's second of four endings⁠—this is super lategame stuff.

You can reach the Petrified Garden by jumping off the teleporter platform while you're in the spacey void warping between zones. The large platform to the side you can dash to is a boss arena⁠—kill the familiar-looking guy here to reawaken the very high-level enemies in the garden.

From there, you can find four god seals scattered through the zone with the Mask of Second Sight. Breaking them all opens a trap door to a secret area below the garden. At the end of the path, you can talk to a mysterious entity behind a sealed gate who spells out the criteria for unlocking endings three and four: Finding all mementos and silver-etched skulls in the game.

They'll also, helpfully, provide a final duck to unlock new items at Umbada's shop. Among this last tranche of material, Umbada will now sell six charms that attach to the Mask of Second Sight. These charms reveal the locations of silver skulls, unopened treasure chests, treasure lizards, Gagi meals, data modules, and Orbewa eggs.

The respective tchotchkes appear as little holographic waypoints onscreen when you're within a few dozen meters of them and wearing the Mask of Second Sight. It can still take some sleuthing to reach the general proximity for these waypoints to appear, and there were some tricky placements that required me to think things through or circumnavigate the level and approach the waypoint from a different direction. But generally, the mask charms changed this collectathon portion of Queen's Domain into another fun part of the experience, rather than a completionist chore.

#3676. Major Esports Tournament Replaced Caster Commentary With AI Voices And It Went Over Very Poorly

Embark Studios, developer of The Finals and organizer of the game’s Grand Major esports tournament, is facing backlash after replacing human casters with AI voices in a highlight reel. IGN reports that the now-deleted video featured footage from the APAC closed qualifiers, but instead of hearing the human casters that actually called the matches, viewers were treated to AI commentators Scotty and June. The incident is rippling through the esports professional community, with some calling for unionization efforts to protect workers.

Proto, one of the casters replaced in the video, spoke out about the incident on social media.

After 4 cycles, open/closed quals, the time, effort, passion and emotion myself @TheeHyperactive and @bluepanda_casts put in. We get replaced by two Ai casters who even quote us :/ I get they are apart of the game but yikes. Thanks @reachthefinals https://t.co/oC8Zb5GrU0

— Proto / Kai (@ProtoANZ) November 16, 2026

Oscar Lundberg, community and competitive operations lead at Embark Studios, apologized for video on social media. “We intended for Scotty and June to help bring more casual interest into The Finals esports ahead of TGM,” he wrote. “That was the goal, but the work of our talent deserved to be included and highlighted, and it wasnât.”

The writing was on the wall indicating that something like this would happen in The Finals. When it launched in 2023, The Finals was called out by players for its use of AI text-to-speech voice acting, something the devs have acknowledged and embraced. “AI text-to-speech is finally extremely powerful,” said Andreas AlmstrÃ¶m, the game’s audio director in Embark Studios’ “Meet The Makers” podcast. “It gets us far enough in terms of quality and allows us to be extremely reactive to new ideas.” Earlier this year, The Finals released Dynamic Commentary, a feature that allows the AI commentator to call out players by name whenever something happens during a match.

Dynamic Commentary is the new feature that will earn you praise from your favorite commentator Scotty, coming in PRIME TIME on Oct. 20!

Live commentary in a live match for the play you just pulled. Now this is what a Game Show is all about!â¦ pic.twitter.com/8acAZGY2Zw

— THE FINALS (@reachthefinals) October 18, 2026

It stands to reason that if a developer is comfortable with using AI-text-to-speech to power the game’s in-universe equivalent of esports casting, they might extend that beyond the confines of the game, possibly to see if anyone would notice or care enough about it. Having in-game AI commentary is the inch, this video experiment is the mile. Thankfully esports professionals, many of whom have lost their jobs over the last six years as studio interest and investment has declined, didn’t let this go by unremarked.

In an interview with IGN, Proto spoke about potential organization efforts to prevent something like this from taking hold in the esports community. “I think industry wide, we definitely need to implement some kind of protection for commentary teams as well as production teams,” he said. “You got to protect those people’s jobs.”

There are few movie franchises as popular as the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which is constantly expanding thanks to new projects arriving in theaters and streaming with a Disney+ subscription. While there's always excitement about upcoming Marvel movies, the Avengers: Doomsday is on another level entirely. The public recently got another look at the Doomsday cast via new posters, and fans aren't holding back their thoughts about one hero's appearance.

What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is limited, which is why fans are devouring every photo, clip, and tidbit of information as they come out. We recently got our best look yet at Alan Cumming's return as Nightcrawler, reprising his role for the first time since 2003's X-2. Check it out below:

First look at Nightcrawler in ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’. https://t.co/78RMOU1SgJNovember 18, 2026
